land.text: the Syr Darya and Amu Darya interfluve, subdued 'around 270 CE' by the Xionites

successors.note: The page adds that the Kangju 'probably became subsumed into the Hephthalites' and gives the infobox end as the 5th century CE.

capitals.name: Beitian (in or near Tashkent)
capitals.note: Pulleyblank: the summer capital, Beitian, 'was in or near modern Tashkent'; the infobox names the capital Kangu; the ruler wintered in Beitian and summered at a steppe headquarters 'a seven days' journey away on horseback' (location unknown).

correction.text: the middle Syr Darya, Tashkent and the Talas basin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row; the page gives no area. 'Their territory covered the region of the Ferghana Valley and the area between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers ... with the core territory along the middle Syr Darya'; Hill places the Kangju in or near the 'Talas basin, Tashkent and Sogdiana'; Zhang Qian visited c. 128 BCE and found a state that 'acknowledges sovereignty to the Yuezhi people in the South and the Xiongnu in the East'. The core is the middle Syr Darya, Tashkent and the Talas; Ferghana and Sogdia are added from 36 BCE.

correction.text: the Kangju core without the Taraz district held by Zhizhi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 44 BCE: Zhizhi settles among the Kangju and builds a fortress; the Kangju city near Taraz is his until the Han take it in 36 BCE (Zhizhi Chanyu page). The Taraz radius is taken out of the core for 44-37 BCE.

correction.text: the Amu Darya-Syr Darya interfluve with the middle Syr Darya, without the Ferghana valley of Dayuan (great-yuan, alive to 50)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'By the Hanshu period, Kangju had "gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana" and controlled five lesser kings'; the page's lead gives the full territory as the Ferghana Valley and the area between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya. The page does not date the gain: 36 BCE is the last dated Kangju-Han event before the Hanshu description (confidence 1 in the ledger). Revised after review: the shape no longer draws Dayuan, the last Cliopatria Great Yuan shape (172 cells), which the great-yuan dossier holds to 50; the Kangju page says only that by the Hanshu period (206 BCE-23 CE) Kangju 'had gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana', so Dayuan comes in at 50, the year great-yuan closes. The page gives no area.

correction.text: the Ferghana Valley and the area between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, with the middle Syr Darya

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe from 50: the -36 shape with Dayuan (the Ferghana valley) added at the year the great-yuan dossier dissolves and names kangju as successor. New keyframe. 'By the Hanshu period, Kangju had "gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana" and controlled five lesser kings'; the page's lead gives the full territory as the Ferghana Valley and the area between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya. The page does not date the gain: 36 BCE is the last dated Kangju-Han event before the Hanshu description (confidence 1 in the ledger). Overlap with the Kushan shapes: Cliopatria's Kushan Empire shape of 51 covers 844 of this shape's 3,035 cells (Sogdia and Ferghana, from kushan-empire ledger 2, confidence 1, 'Cliopatria's reading only'); the Kangju page, which has the Kangju in control of Dayuan and Sogdiana until about 270 CE, is followed and the land is kept here (see notes: sa-02 should drop kushan ledger 2).

region.text: the middle Syr Darya, Tashkent and the Talas

ledger.note: c. 128 BCE: Zhang Qian finds the Kangju state. 'Zhang Qian visited the area c. 128 BCE'; Kangju 'acknowledges sovereignty to the Yuezhi people in the South and the Xiongnu in the East'. The infobox gives '1st century BCE (?)' for the founding; the first dated sight is used.

region.text: the Kangju city near Taraz and the Dulaishui fortress

ledger.note: 44 BCE: Zhizhi Chanyu settles among the Kangju. He 'made a marriage alliance with the rulers of Kangju near Lake Balkhash' and later 'forced the Kangju people to build him a fortress on the Dulaishui River' (undated); the city the Han reached in 36 BCE was 'around modern Taraz'. The Kangju page has the Kangju ruler giving his daughter to Zhizhi. [Reviewer ia-01-x, 2026-10-19] The Zhizhi Chanyu page dates only 'In 44 BCE he was reported to be on the north slope of the Tian Shan' and the start of the westward move to 49 BCE; the arrival in Kangju is undated, so the year is a reading.

36 BCE: the Han kill Zhizhi at the Kangju city. 'Han generals Chen Tang and Gan Yanshou led a force of 40,000'; 'Upon reaching Kangju (around modern Taraz)' they took the city and Zhizhi was killed and decapitated; the Kangju page adds that the Kangju ruler 'was subsequently forced to send his son as a hostage to the Han court'.

c. 36 BCE: Kangju holds Sogdiana (bridge). The Hanshu-period description has Kangju 'had gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana' with 'five lesser kings' (Kangju page: 'By the time of the Hanshu (which covers the period from 206 BCE to 23 CE)'); the page gives no year (confidence 1; 36 BCE bridges to the Hanshu). Dayuan is no longer taken from nobody: see the 50 gain from great-yuan.

region.text: Dayuan, the last Great Yuan shape, the Ferghana valley

ledger.note: c. 50: Dayuan passes to the Kangju. 'By this time it had gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana in which it controlled "five lesser kings"' (Kangju page, Hanshu period 206 BCE-23 CE); the page gives no year, so 50 is the year the great-yuan dossier closes and names kangju as its successor for Fergana (Cliopatria's last Great Yuan shape, 43). Replaces the earlier gain of Dayuan from nobody in 36 BCE; a vassal reading ('five lesser kings') is possible but undated.

c. 270: the Xionites subdue the Kangju. 'Around 270 CE they were subdued by the Xionites'; the infobox ends the Kangju in the 5th century CE and the page says they 'probably became subsumed into the Hephthalites'. The xionites dossier (ia-01) starts in 353, not 270: the Xionite counterpart is the page's; its owner can decide whether to start earlier, otherwise this counterpart should read nobody.

wars.name: Han campaign against Dayuan (Kangju as ally)
wars.outcome: 'In 101 BCE, the Kangju allied with Dayuan against the Han.' The page gives no battle and no border change.

wars.name: Han expedition against Zhizhi
wars.outcome: Chen Tang and Gan Yanshou, with 40,000 men, took the Kangju city near Taraz, killed Zhizhi and sent his head to Chang'an; the Kangju ruler's son was later sent as hostage to the Han.
wars.note: A Kangju relief force made several night attacks on the Han camp.

wars.name: Xionite conquest of the Kangju
wars.outcome: Around 270 CE the Kangju were subdued by the Xionites.

certainty.note: The page gives a region (the Ferghana Valley, the Amu Darya-Syr Darya interfluve, the middle Syr Darya) and a city, never a frontier.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Kangju). The infobox (Established '1st century BCE (?)', Disestablished '5th century CE') disagrees with the page's dated sentences (c. 128 BCE sighting; 'around 270 CE' subdued by the Xionites): the dossier uses the dated sentences. The 'five lesser kings' and the dependent states around 125 CE (Yancai, identified with the Aorsi, and Yan) are inside or beyond the drawn shape and are not given separate land; Yancai's subjection is dated to the 1st century BCE by Zadneprovskiy. The Kangju paid tribute to the Yuezhi and the Xiongnu (the yuezhi and xiongnu dossiers should carry the vassal_start; not checked). The zhizhi-xiongnu dossier (ia-01-a) mirrors the 44 BCE and 36 BCE events with the same Taraz radius. The page has the Kangju 'established themselves in Chach' (Pulleyblank) and links the Kangju to Sogdians, so the Sogdian city-states (a counterpart name in other dossiers) are folded here. Gazetteer names used (Chach, Sogdia, Fergana, Transoxiana, Taraz, the Kazakhstan oblasts) all resolve. REVISED after review (ia-01-x fix pass). DOUBLE-DRAW: the -36 keyframe used to draw Dayuan (great-yuan, alive to 50, wholly inside it) and, from 51, 844 of its 3,035 cells (about 213,000 km2: Sogdia and Ferghana) lie inside Cliopatria's Kushan Empire shapes. Dayuan is now left out until 50 and gained from great-yuan that year (great-yuan's dissolve has counterpart null and should name kangju). Kushan: this dossier KEEPS the land and does not subtract the Kushan shape, because the Kangju page has the Kangju in control of Dayuan and Sogdiana and subdued only around 270 CE, while the kushan-empire dossier's own note says its 51 gain of Fergana and Sogdia (ledger 2, confidence 1) is 'Cliopatria's reading only: the Kushan page opened has nothing on Ferghana or Dayuan'; sa-02 should drop kushan ledger 2 and the Fergana-Sogdia land from its 51 keyframe. Until it does, the map double-draws that land from 51 to 237. The Zhizhi settlement year (44 BCE) is a reading, not the page's (reviewer note kept). 270: the Kangju page names the Xionites, whose dossier starts in 353 (identity 353..401); listed for the xionites owner. The Yuezhi/Xiongnu tributary ties ('acknowledges sovereignty to the Yuezhi people in the South and the Xiongnu in the East', Zhang Qian c. 128 BCE; also 'tributiaries' undated) are not drawn as events: the page dates neither their start nor their end, and the validator wants a dated end; the yuezhi and xiongnu owners can add vassal events. The page's 'Kangju-Kushans' irrigation sentence is cultural, not territorial. Great Yuan region used is the Cliopatria shape (172 cells), not the gazetteer 'Fergana' region (411 cells); the 277 extra Fergana cells stay in the shape from -36.
